questions.question: You must ensure that all internet-bound traffic from Subnet1 passes through a firewall appliance that has the private IP address 10.0.2.4. What should you create and associate with Subnet1?

options.text: A route table that contains a route for 0.0.0.0/0 with the next hop type Virtual appliance and the next hop address 10.0.2.4
options.why: Correct. The user-defined route overrides the default system route to the internet.

options.text: A route table that contains a route for 0.0.0.0/0 with the next hop type Internet
options.why: This matches the default system route and does not send traffic to the firewall.

options.text: A network security group that denies outbound Internet traffic
options.why: An NSG can block traffic but cannot redirect it to the firewall.

options.text: A service endpoint for Microsoft.Network
options.why: Service endpoints apply to Azure PaaS services and do not redirect internet traffic.

questions.explanation: Associate a route table with the subnet and use the Virtual appliance next hop type with the private IP address of the appliance.

questions.question: A subnet has the following effective routes: 10.0.0.0/8 next hop None, 10.2.0.0/16 next hop Virtual appliance 10.0.2.4, and 0.0.0.0/0 next hop Internet. Where is a packet to 10.2.5.9 sent?

options.text: To the virtual appliance at 10.0.2.4
options.why: Correct. 10.2.0.0/16 is the longest prefix that matches.

options.text: It is dropped
options.why: The 10.0.0.0/8 route also matches, but the /16 route is more specific.

options.text: To the internet
options.why: 0.0.0.0/0 matches every address but has the shortest prefix.

options.text: To the virtual network gateway
options.why: No route with that next hop matches the destination.

questions.explanation: Azure selects the route with the longest prefix match. On an identical prefix, a user-defined route is preferred over BGP and system routes.

questions.question: You create a route table that contains a route to a network virtual appliance (NVA). Traffic from the subnet reaches the NVA, but the NVA does not forward it. What should you configure?

options.text: Enable IP forwarding on the network interface of the NVA
options.why: Correct. Without IP forwarding, Azure drops traffic that is not addressed to the NVA.

options.text: Disable gateway route propagation on the route table
options.why: Route propagation affects BGP routes from a gateway, not forwarding by the NVA.

options.text: Associate the route table with the network interface of the NVA
options.why: Route tables are associated with subnets, not network interfaces.

options.text: Add an inbound NAT rule
options.why: Inbound NAT rules belong to load balancers and do not enable forwarding.

questions.explanation: An NVA requires IP forwarding on its Azure network interface and in its operating system.

questions.question: Which two statements about route tables are true? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: A route table can be associated with multiple subnets.
options.why: Correct. One route table can serve many subnets.

options.text: A subnet can be associated with only one route table.
options.why: Correct. Each subnet has zero or one route table.

options.text: A route table can be associated directly with a network interface.
options.why: Route tables are associated with subnets.

options.text: A route table can be associated with a subnet in a different region.
options.why: The route table must be in the same region and subscription as the virtual network.

questions.explanation: Route tables are associated with subnets in the same region and subscription.

questions.question: Subnet1 must not be able to send any traffic to the address range 172.16.50.0/24. You must use routing to meet the requirement. Which next hop type should you use in the user-defined route?

options.text: None
options.why: Correct. Traffic that matches a route with the next hop type None is dropped.

options.text: Virtual network
options.why: This keeps traffic inside the virtual network.

options.text: Internet
options.why: This sends traffic to the internet.

options.text: Virtual network gateway
options.why: This sends traffic to the VPN or ExpressRoute gateway.

questions.explanation: The None next hop type drops traffic to the destination prefix.
